title: Familie und der Akkusativ
summary: Family vocabulary plus the accusative case — only the masculine article moves

blocks.title: Familie: der, die, das — und der Akkusativ
blocks.body: Family words each have their own gender: **der Bruder** (brother), **die Schwester** (sister), **das Kind** (child). Here's the twist: when the family member is the **object** of a sentence — *ich habe…* — only the **masculine** article changes: **der → den**, **ein → einen**. Feminine and neuter stay exactly the same. So *ich habe einen Bruder*, but *ich habe eine Schwester* and *ich habe ein Kind* — no change there at all.
blocks.callout: Merk dir: nur maskulin bewegt sich. Just the 'der' words move.

blocks.title: Subject vs. object — watch the masculine

pairs.note: Same word, but 'einen' only shows up when the brother is the object.

blocks.prompt: Wie sagt man 'I have a brother'?
blocks.explain: *Bruder* is masculine, so the accusative after *haben* is *einen Bruder*.

blocks.prompt: Give the accusative: 'a brother' (as in ich habe ___).
blocks.explain: *einen Bruder* — masculine nouns take -en in the accusative.
